data.content_ref: inline:SRC_005 and SRC_001 are compatible via shared mechanism: both frame the $6 answer as the artifact of a constructed pedagogical exercise that hides a proportional axiom. SRC_005 identifies the hidden axiom as a covering principle (uniform pricing) tested as a reasoning skill; SRC_001 identifies it as strict linearity stipulated away by construction. Their shared mechanism is pedagogical concealment of an axiom, and they are compatible because one emphasizes skill-recognition while the other emphasizes assumption-stipulation, with no contradiction. This relation is refuted if the two artifacts' mechanisms are merely described side-by-side without naming the shared predicate (concealment of an axiom by construction), or if they actually contradict on whether the axiom is a reasoning skill versus a stipulation — a summary of the endpoints is not a relation.
